title: OpenClaw Operating Card
summary: Operate OpenClaw as a self-hosted agent gateway with explicit channels, tools, sandboxing, credentials, health checks, and rollback.
prerequisites: A supported Node.js and operating-system path
A host and channel security boundary

sections.title: Treat the gateway as an operational service
paragraphs: OpenClaw is a self-hosted gateway that connects agent runtimes, tools, skills, plugins, and communication channels. Choose it when you are prepared to operate identities, credentials, host access, sessions, updates, and channel policy as a service.

The model sees only capabilities that survive the configured profile, allow and deny policy, sandbox, provider restrictions, channel permissions, and installed plugins. Review every layer instead of relying on one allowlist.

sections.title: Install deliberately and verify the gateway boundary
paragraphs: Confirm current platform requirements, review installer behavior, pin an update channel where required, and run documented health checks. Bind interfaces and channel identities according to the intended threat model.
Enable only required tools, skills, plugins, and channels. Keep provider and channel credentials external to prompts and repositories, and maintain an export, update, rollback, and uninstall plan.

code.label: OpenClaw operating card
code.code:
Task: [one agent or gateway outcome]
Scope: [host, workspace, channels, and sessions]
Permissions: [tools, plugins, sandbox, network, and identities]
Credentials: [approved secret stores and rotation owners]
Health checks: [version, doctor, gateway, and channel tests]
Verification: [observable result and audit evidence]
Recovery: [disable route/tool, restore config, rotate, rollback]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes version and installation path, effective config, enabled capabilities, identity and channel map, health results, and a tested user-boundary outcome without secret values.

If behavior or access is unexpected, disable the affected channel or tool, preserve logs safely, rotate exposed credentials, restore the last reviewed configuration, and rerun health and end-to-end checks.

sections.title: Your first OpenClaw task: a local-only chat
paragraphs: In this lab you will configure OpenClaw as a local gateway, select Mistral explicitly, verify the gateway boundary, and send one harmless chat prompt. You will then complete a separate offline Python configuration-review exercise. The Python checker is an educational subset. It is not OpenClaw's schema validator or security enforcement.

This artifact does not claim that an agent, provider, gateway, approval, or live completion has been observed. A real provider completion may use the network and provider credits. Offline tests make no model calls. No external messaging channel or personal messaging account is needed.

code.label: Scope card
code.code:
In scope: isolated local gateway, Mistral onboarding, version capture, validation, status, security audit, harmless first chat, offline reviewer exercise
Out of scope: external channels, service installation, personal messaging, autonomous file changes, commit, deployment, and secret capture

sections.title: Confirm the host and preserve the boundary
paragraphs: The OpenClaw getting-started documentation observed on 2026-09-20 lists Node.js 24.16 or later, or 26.1 or later, and recommends Node.js 26. Source: https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started

Use one personal, mutually trusted local boundary for this lab. OpenClaw's security documentation describes one trusted boundary per gateway rather than hostile multi-tenant isolation, and documents loopback as the host default. Source: https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security

Keep mutable OpenClaw state and configuration outside the exercise repository. Never put a real API key or gateway token in a command argument, prompt, repository, screenshot, or captured output. A passing test does not authorize a commit or deployment.

code.label: Bash, version capture
code.code:
node --version
openclaw --version
python3 --version
# Record non-secret output in private lab notes only.

sections.title: Create isolated paths without overwriting files
paragraphs: OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR isolates OpenClaw state and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH selects the configuration path. Source: https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started

Run this from the directory where you want the lab state. It preflights the root and every target path before creating anything. If any path exists, it stops without changing that path. The printed paths are examples from your machine, not a claim about a live run.

code.label: setup_paths.py
code.code:
from pathlib import Path

root = Path.cwd() / "openclaw-first-task-state"
state = root / "state"
config = root / "openclaw.json"

# Preflight every path before creating any directory or file.
existing = [path for path in (root, state, config) if path.exists()]
if existing:
    joined = ", ".join(str(path) for path in existing)
    raise SystemExit("Refusing to use existing lab paths: " + joined)

root.mkdir()
state.mkdir()
print("OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=" + str(state.resolve()))
print("OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=" + str(config.resolve()))
print("Set both values in the same shell used for OpenClaw.")

sections.title: Set the isolated paths in your shell
paragraphs: Set the variables in the shell that will run onboarding, validation, the gateway, and the first chat. The values below are examples. Replace them with the paths printed by setup_paths.py.

sections.title: PowerShell path setup
paragraphs: PowerShell uses the same two environment variables. Set them in the current session before running OpenClaw.

sections.title: Install and select the Mistral provider
paragraphs: Install the documented Mistral provider plugin, then use the classic onboarding wizard with the Mistral API-key choice. The wizard prompts for the key, so the key is not placed in a command argument. Source: https://docs.openclaw.ai/providers/mistral

List the models returned by your installation. The documentation gives mistral/mistral-large-latest as an example, not an availability guarantee. Treat the command's output and any provider error as the result for your installation.

code.label: Provider installation and onboarding
code.code:
openclaw plugins install @openclaw/mistral-provider
openclaw onboard --classic --auth-choice mistral-api-key
openclaw models list --provider mistral

sections.title: Apply the documented local-only baseline
paragraphs: The hardened baseline documented on 2026-09-20 uses gateway.mode local, gateway.bind loopback, gateway.auth.mode token, and gateway.port 18789. It also uses the messaging profile, denies the listed automation, runtime, filesystem, and session tools, restricts filesystem access to the workspace, sets execution security to deny and execution prompting to always, disables elevated tools and agent-to-agent access, limits session visibility to the agent, and scopes direct messages per channel and peer. Source: https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security/hardened-baseline

The exact paths are tools.sessions.visibility, tools.agentToAgent.enabled, and session.dmScope. Do not use sessions.visibility, sessions.agentToAgent.enabled, or sessions.dmScope. Let onboarding handle the gateway token through its secure flow. Do not display, copy, or store a token in this lab.

config set uses path and value arguments. With --strict-json --dry-run, each command validates the proposed post-change configuration without applying it. Only after every dry run succeeds should you run the corresponding command without --dry-run. The apply commands below preserve unrelated settings because they target individual paths. Source: https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/config

The expected applied result is the documented set of values shown by these commands. It is not a claim that they succeeded on your machine. Record the actual exit status and non-secret output from every dry run, apply, and final validation.

code.label: Dry-run every value, then apply the same values
code.code:
openclaw config file

# Phase 1: validate every proposed change without writing it.
openclaw config set gateway.mode '"local"' --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set gateway.bind '"loopback"' --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set gateway.port 18789 --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set gateway.auth.mode '"token"' --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set tools.profile '"messaging"' --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set tools.deny '["group:automation","group:runtime","group:fs","sessions_spawn","sessions_send"]' --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set tools.fs.workspaceOnly true --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set tools.exec.security '"deny"' --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set tools.exec.ask '"always"' --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set tools.elevated.enabled false --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set tools.sessions.visibility '"agent"' --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set tools.agentToAgent.enabled false --strict-json --dry-run
openclaw config set session.dmScope '"per-channel-peer"' --strict-json --dry-run

# Stop here if any dry run fails. Otherwise apply the identical values.
openclaw config set gateway.mode '"local"' --strict-json
openclaw config set gateway.bind '"loopback"' --strict-json
openclaw config set gateway.port 18789 --strict-json
openclaw config set gateway.auth.mode '"token"' --strict-json
openclaw config set tools.profile '"messaging"' --strict-json
openclaw config set tools.deny '["group:automation","group:runtime","group:fs","sessions_spawn","sessions_send"]' --strict-json
openclaw config set tools.fs.workspaceOnly true --strict-json
openclaw config set tools.exec.security '"deny"' --strict-json
openclaw config set tools.exec.ask '"always"' --strict-json
openclaw config set tools.elevated.enabled false --strict-json
openclaw config set tools.sessions.visibility '"agent"' --strict-json
openclaw config set tools.agentToAgent.enabled false --strict-json
openclaw config set session.dmScope '"per-channel-peer"' --strict-json

openclaw config validate --json

sections.title: Validate the configuration and diagnose malformed input safely
paragraphs: config file prints the active configuration path. config validate --json checks the installed schema without starting the gateway, but it cannot establish whether provider parameters or credentials work. config patch --file expects a config-shaped object, not a JSON Patch array. Source observed on 2026-09-20: https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/config

The first command below proposes a list where tools.exec.security requires the scalar string deny. Because it includes --dry-run, it must not apply the proposed change. The expected result is rejection by the installed schema and no configuration mutation. This is an expected result, not a claimed live outcome. If it is unexpectedly accepted, stop and preserve the command output and installed OpenClaw version for investigation. Do not apply the malformed value.

The recovery is deliberately narrow. Dry-run the documented deny value, apply it only if that dry run succeeds, and validate the complete installed schema. A successful schema validation still does not prove that a provider credential works, that a model is available, or that the gateway is safe for hostile multi-tenant use.

code.label: Malformed dry run, narrow recovery, and validation
code.code:
openclaw config file

# Expected: rejected, nonzero status, and no write because this is a dry run.
openclaw config set tools.exec.security '[]' --strict-json --dry-run
printf 'malformed dry-run exit status: %s\n' "$?"

# Recovery: validate the correct scalar before applying it.
openclaw config set tools.exec.security '"deny"' --strict-json --dry-run
# Run the next command only if the preceding dry run succeeded.
openclaw config set tools.exec.security '"deny"' --strict-json
openclaw config validate --json

# Record actual outputs. Do not report the expected rejection as an observed result.

sections.title: Run gateway health checks without installing a service
paragraphs: Use two terminals for this workflow. Set the isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH values in Terminal A before running these commands. Use the same already-existing values in Terminal B. Do not rerun path setup or onboarding in Terminal B.

Terminal A: validate the active configuration and security boundaries first. Then start the gateway in the foreground. The documented equivalent forms are openclaw gateway and openclaw gateway run. The running guide states that gateway.mode must be local, that the foreground process stops on SIGINT or SIGTERM, and that no service installation is required: https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/gateway/running

The gateway command blocks the Terminal A shell. Do not place the Terminal B commands after it in the same shell and expect them to run. Leave Terminal A running. Open Terminal B, set the same isolated environment values, verify the active configuration path, and run status or dashboard only after Terminal A shows that the foreground gateway is running. Keep Terminal A open until you press Ctrl+C to shut the gateway down.

A successful validation, security audit, status display, or dashboard display does not prove that a provider credential works or that a model completion will succeed. This lab does not claim a live health success, observed model route, or successful provider call. Do not expose the gateway beyond loopback, install a service, auto-approve doctor fixes, or print a token.

code.label: Terminal A, then Terminal B
code.code:
# Terminal A: use the isolated values established in the earlier environment section.
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="/absolute/path/openclaw-first-task-state/state"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="/absolute/path/openclaw-first-task-state/openclaw.json"
printf '%s\n' "$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR" "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"

openclaw config file
openclaw config validate --json
openclaw security audit

# This is a foreground, blocking process. Keep Terminal A open.
# The documented equivalent is: openclaw gateway
openclaw gateway run

# Terminal B: open a separate terminal after Terminal A is running.
# Set the same existing isolated values. Do not rerun setup_paths.py or onboarding.
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="/absolute/path/openclaw-first-task-state/state"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="/absolute/path/openclaw-first-task-state/openclaw.json"
printf '%s\n' "$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR" "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"

# Verify the active isolated configuration path, then inspect the running gateway.
openclaw config file
openclaw status
# Optional alternative inspection in Terminal B:
# openclaw dashboard

# Return to Terminal A and press Ctrl+C for SIGINT shutdown.

sections.title: Create the offline configuration-review exercise
paragraphs: This separate Python exercise reviews a fictional OpenClaw-shaped dictionary. It follows the documented nesting for gateway.auth and tools.elevated, but it does not load OpenClaw, call a provider, validate the installed schema, or enforce permissions. Its finite contract requires local mode, loopback binding, token authentication, workspace-only filesystem access, execution security deny, execution prompting always, disabled elevation, and no configured external channels.

The setup contains an intentionally faulty reviewer and eight protected tests. Do not edit the tests to make the reviewer pass. The script preflights the lab root and every target path before creating anything. If any target exists, it exits before creation. Run it from the parent directory in which you want the new openclaw-config-review directory.

code.label: create_lab.py
code.code:
from pathlib import Path

root = Path.cwd() / "openclaw-config-review"
reviewer_path = root / "reviewer.py"
test_path = root / "test_reviewer.py"
fixture_path = root / "fixtures.json"
targets = (root, reviewer_path, test_path, fixture_path)

existing = [path for path in targets if path.exists()]
if existing:
    joined = ", ".join(str(path) for path in existing)
    raise SystemExit("Refusing to overwrite existing lab paths: " + joined)

reviewer = '''def is_safe(config):
    # Intentionally faulty: mutates input, assumes nested shapes,
    # accepts security="ask", and ignores tools.exec.ask.
    gateway = config.setdefault("gateway", {})
    gateway["bind"] = gateway.get("bind", "loopback")
    tools = config["tools"]
    return (
        gateway["mode"] == "local"
        and gateway["bind"] == "loopback"
        and gateway["auth"]["mode"] == "token"
        and tools["fs"]["workspaceOnly"] is True
        and tools["exec"]["security"] in ("deny", "ask")
        and tools["elevated"]["enabled"] is False
        and config.get("channels", {}) == {}
    )
'''

tests = '''import copy
import unittest
from reviewer import is_safe

SAFE = {
    "gateway": {
        "mode": "local",
        "bind": "loopback",
        "auth": {"mode": "token"},
    },
    "tools": {
        "fs": {"workspaceOnly": True},
        "exec": {"security": "deny", "ask": "always"},
        "elevated": {"enabled": False},
    },
}

class ReviewerTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_safe_fixture(self):
        self.assertTrue(is_safe(copy.deepcopy(SAFE)))

    def test_public_bind_is_rejected(self):
        value = copy.deepcopy(SAFE)
        value["gateway"]["bind"] = "0.0.0.0"
        self.assertFalse(is_safe(value))

    def test_malformed_gateway_auth_is_rejected_without_exception(self):
        value = copy.deepcopy(SAFE)
        value["gateway"]["auth"] = []
        self.assertFalse(is_safe(value))

    def test_security_ask_is_rejected(self):
        value = copy.deepcopy(SAFE)
        value["tools"]["exec"]["security"] = "ask"
        self.assertFalse(is_safe(value))

    def test_exec_ask_must_be_always(self):
        value = copy.deepcopy(SAFE)
        value["tools"]["exec"]["ask"] = "never"
        self.assertFalse(is_safe(value))

    def test_malformed_tools_is_rejected_without_exception(self):
        value = copy.deepcopy(SAFE)
        value["tools"] = []
        self.assertFalse(is_safe(value))

    def test_malformed_security_is_rejected_without_exception(self):
        value = copy.deepcopy(SAFE)
        value["tools"]["exec"]["security"] = []
        self.assertFalse(is_safe(value))

    def test_input_is_not_mutated(self):
        value = {"gateway": {"mode": "local"}}
        before = copy.deepcopy(value)
        try:
            is_safe(value)
        except (KeyError, TypeError):
            pass
        self.assertEqual(value, before)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
'''

fixture = '{"purpose":"fictional educational fixture; not an OpenClaw schema"}\n'

# All paths were checked before this first creation step.
root.mkdir()
for path, content in (
    (reviewer_path, reviewer),
    (test_path, tests),
    (fixture_path, fixture),
):
    with path.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(content)

print("Created", root)
print("Run: python -m unittest discover -s openclaw-config-review -p 'test_*.py' -v")

sections.title: Run the faulty reviewer and identify the concrete failures
paragraphs: Run the suite from the parent directory. The initial implementation is expected to run eight tests and end with FAILED (failures=3, errors=2). This count is derived from the supplied code, not presented as a live execution result. The actual output remains UNKNOWN until you run it.

The two expected errors have a common cause: the reviewer indexes malformed gateway.auth and tools values as though they were dictionaries. The three expected failures have distinct causes: it accepts security="ask", ignores tools.exec.ask="never", and mutates an incomplete gateway by inserting bind="loopback" before later failing.

The recovery scope is reviewer.py only. Keep test_reviewer.py and fixtures.json unchanged so the tests continue to protect the contract. Record a different count or failure set exactly as observed rather than replacing it with the expected output.

code.label: Baseline command and expected summary
code.code:
python -m unittest discover -s openclaw-config-review -p 'test_*.py' -v

# Expected from the intentionally faulty source, not a claimed live result:
# Ran 8 tests
# FAILED (failures=3, errors=2)
# Actual result: UNKNOWN until this command is run.

sections.title: Replace only the faulty reviewer
paragraphs: Replace only openclaw-config-review/reviewer.py with the complete reference below. Do not change the protected tests, the fictional fixture, OpenClaw configuration, provider state, or gateway state. Restoring a source file would not reverse an external effect such as a provider charge or a sent message.

This implementation accepts only JSON-like dictionary, list, string, number, Boolean, and null shapes relevant to the exercise. It checks every required container before nested access, checks Boolean fields by exact type, requires tools.exec.security to equal deny, and separately requires tools.exec.ask to equal always. It accepts an omitted channels key as no configured channels, rejects channels=null, returns False for malformed configuration values, and does not mutate its input.

After replacement, the expected result is eight passing tests and OK. That remains an expected local result until the learner runs the command. It does not establish any property of an installed OpenClaw gateway.

code.label: openclaw-config-review/reviewer.py, complete corrected reference

sections.title: Independent task: add exact port review without changing is_safe
paragraphs: Complete this task before reading the feedback section. Keep the corrected is_safe function and all eight original tests unchanged. Add a separate review(config, required_port=18789) function to reviewer.py. This is a changed requirement because is_safe does not inspect gateway.port.

The new function has a finite contract. First, required_port itself must have exact type int, so bool is invalid, and must be from 1 through 65535 inclusive. Invalid required_port values must raise ValueError with exactly: required_port must be an integer from 1 through 65535. For a valid required_port, review must return False rather than raise when config is malformed, when is_safe(config) is false, when gateway.port is absent, when the configured port is a bool, list, dictionary, or out of range, or when it does not match required_port. It returns True only when the original safety contract passes and gateway.port is an exact integer in range that equals required_port. It must not mutate config.

Save the following as openclaw-config-review/test_port_review.py without modifying test_reviewer.py. With only the corrected first reference present, the combined discovery run has 16 test methods. The actual pre-implementation result reports 17 errors, not 8: unittest counts the 16 methods in its Ran line, while cases created by with self.subTest() are reported as additional individual error entries. This is an expected pre-implementation result, not a claimed run. After implementing review, all sixteen test methods are expected to pass.

code.label: openclaw-config-review/test_port_review.py

sections.title: Causal feedback and complete changed-task answer
paragraphs: Consult this section only after attempting the changed-input task. Append the function below to openclaw-config-review/reviewer.py. Do not replace or edit is_safe, test_reviewer.py, or test_port_review.py.

Validation of required_port occurs first because it is a caller contract rather than untrusted configuration content. Exact type checking rejects True and False even though Python treats bool as a subclass of int. The range check permits the inclusive boundaries 1 and 65535. Once required_port is valid, calling is_safe preserves every original requirement. The gateway container is then safe to read, but gateway.port still receives its own exact-type, range, and equality checks.

These causes map directly to the tests: a missing port produces None and returns False; bool, list, and dictionary values fail exact integer checking; 0 and 65536 fail the range; a valid but different integer fails equality; and invalid required_port values raise the specified ValueError. Neither function writes to config, so the mutation test passes.

Before appending the function, the expected combined result is sixteen test methods with 17 reported errors, not eight errors. The extra reports come from subTest cases within three test methods, which unittest reports separately. After appending it, the expected result is sixteen passing test methods and OK. Actual results remain UNKNOWN until run. Passing these tests proves only the stated educational contract and does not validate OpenClaw, start a gateway, authorize a provider call, or grant permission to commit or deploy.

code.label: Append this function to reviewer.py, then run both suites

sections.title: Stop the gateway and preserve non-secret evidence
paragraphs: Press Ctrl+C in the foreground gateway terminal before changing configuration or recovering source. Preserve only non-secret evidence: versions, paths, command outcomes, the harmless prompt, the response if permitted, and changed-file names. Do not capture API keys, gateway tokens, authorization headers, or secret-bearing configuration.

The original scope remains a local-only first chat plus an offline configuration-review exercise. If a live provider, local chat, or gateway result was not checked, record CANNOT VERIFY and state what would establish it. Never assume a source rollback reverses external effects.
